status_summary: No change from Federal Credit Reform Act accounting to fair-value accounting was found. Public Law 119-21, signed on 2025-07-04, added a program earnings test for Direct Loan eligibility rather than a requirement that institutions share loan losses. A House reconciliation proposal that would have required colleges to reimburse a share of unpaid loans was reported in June 2025, and the Senate committee text replaced it with an earnings-based metric. The Department's final earnings rule was published on 2026-07-01 (91 FR 40136); its Part 685 changes take effect 2026-08-31 and the remaining provisions take effect 2027-07-01.

timeline.event: Public Law 119-21 was signed; its section 84001 created a program-level earnings test for Direct Loan eligibility, and the Congressional Research Service summary of its Higher Education Act amendments does not mention institutional risk sharing or fair-value accounting.

The Department of Education published a final rule (91 FR 40136) implementing the earnings provisions of Public Law 119-21 through an earnings premium test; it is not a risk-sharing or fair-value measure.

title: Fair-value accounting for federal student loans and institutional risk sharing
uncertainties: The final rule was read through about 100,000 of its 138,000 characters on the Federal Register site, with no mention of the Federal Credit Reform Act, fair value or loss sharing in that portion. The body text of section 84001 of Public Law 119-21 was cut off on govinfo (table of contents only), so its content rests on the rule's and CRS's descriptions. The House risk-sharing proposal is described in a public-radio report and a trustees association comparison; its House text and vote were not read from a primary source, so it is not entered as a timeline event. The CRS text read was truncated, so risk sharing in omitted sections is not excluded. The Congressional Budget Office publishes credit estimates including fair-value measures as part of its own analysis; that is not a government accounting change and was not used as an event. No OMB, Treasury or Department change to loan accounting was found in the FY2027 budget summary text read. Standalone bills on risk sharing in the 119th Congress were searched once and none were confirmed. The repayment, subsidy and borrowing-limit features of the single-program recommendation are outside this record. c11-08 lists this element as unchecked; this record owns it.
